big: Meena's jeweller shows her a price board: ₹X for a gram. The same gram in London, converted to rupees, is a bit less. The gap is not a trick. It is duty, tax and the rupee, all at work.

lines: Why did gold rise this month, when nothing special happened in India?
Gold is priced in dollars across the world. Your rupee price moves with the global price, with the rupee-dollar rate, and with duties and taxes at home.

alt: Bars showing the rupee price of gold rising ten percent when the rupee weakens and the dollar price is unchanged
caps: The global dollar price of gold does not change.
The rupee weakens from 80 to 88 against the dollar.
The rupee price of gold rises by 10%.
Made-up numbers to show the idea. A weaker rupee lifts the gold price at home.

rows: Interest less inflation. Higher real rates make gold less attractive
A weaker rupee raises the rupee price
Make the local price higher than the converted global price
note: Gold pays no interest, so when real interest rates rise, holding it costs more in missed income.

q: The global price of gold is unchanged, but the rupee weakens against the dollar. What happens to the rupee price of gold?
why: A weaker rupee does not lower the rupee price.
The rupee price changes with the exchange rate.
A price does not fall to zero because of the exchange rate.
Gold is priced in dollars, so a weaker rupee lifts its price in rupees.

q: Real interest rates rise well above inflation. What is the likely effect on gold?
opts: It becomes more attractive for sure
why: Higher real rates tend to reduce gold's appeal for sure.
When bonds pay more in real terms, gold's lack of income hurts.
Rates are one of the main forces that act on gold.
Gold never starts paying interest to its holders.

q: Why is the local jeweller's price usually higher than the global price converted to rupees?
opts: Import duty and GST are added
The price is set by the weather
why: A jeweller follows a market rate and does not guess it.
SEBI does not add a charge to the price of gold.
India adds import duty and GST, so the local price is higher.
Weather does not set the price of gold.

q: Several central banks add tonnes of gold to their reserves. What does this usually do?
opts: It crashes the price at once
It changes the purity of gold
why: Heavy purchases by central banks add steady demand.
More demand tends to support the price and not crash it.
Trading goes on as usual when central banks buy.
Buying has nothing to do with purity.

pts: Gold is priced in dollars, so a weaker rupee lifts its rupee price.
Higher real interest rates make gold less attractive.
Duty and GST make local prices higher.
